DEBUG
SYMPTOM: Hook scripts running `tty` returned "not a tty" because stdin is piped. Stored tty never matched iTerm2's tty paths (e.g. /dev/ttys004).
CAUSE: `tty` reads /proc/self/fd/0 which is a pipe when stdin is redirected. The hook subprocess has no controlling terminal.
FIX: Use `ps -o tty= -p $PPID` to get the PARENT process (Claude Code)'s tty, then prepend /dev/: `TTY_PATH=$(ps -o tty= -p $PPID 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); [ -n "$TTY_PATH" ] && TTY_PATH="/dev/$TTY_PATH"`
PREVENT: Any hook script that needs the terminal tty must use the PPID approach. `tty` will always fail in hook subprocesses.

WHERE: ~/.claude/hooks/pixel-office-session-start.sh, ~/.claude/hooks/pixel-office-pre-tool-use.sh
GOTCHA: Also need to validate stored tty values — updateSessionTty() must reject strings that don't start with /dev/ (to avoid storing stale "not a tty" values)
